subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in scheduler/config surface for per-agent or per-group foreground command lanes, and what default plus global-cap semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution adds public config and scheduler behavior across agent, channel, hook, and subagent surfaces; ClawSweeper should not choose that product contract automatically.

options.title: Design opt-in core lane policy
options.body: Keep `main` as the default, add maintainer-approved per-agent or per-group lane config, and include a global safety cap plus docs/tests.

options.title: Defer to narrow lane surfaces
options.body: Let hook, channel, browser, and subagent lane proposals land independently without adding a top-level per-agent foreground contract yet.

options.title: Document separate gateways only
options.body: Keep foreground replies on the shared `main` lane and recommend separate gateway deployments for heavy agent groups.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core lane policy
recommendation.body: Keep `main` as the default, add maintainer-approved per-agent or per-group lane config, and include a global safety cap plus docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal for lane and config concurrency code points to steipete, and the decision affects core scheduler defaults.
